classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish direct and inverse gas models, calculate constants and convert cubic metres to cubic centimetres before rounding.

content.prompt: If a gas behaves in an ideal way then the relationship between pressure, volume and temperature can be approximated with simple equations.

children.label: a
children.prompt: When the gas is kept at a constant pressure, the volume $V$ it occupies varies directly with its temperature $T$ when that is expressed in Kelvin instead of Celsius.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Write down an equation relating $V$ and $T$.

answer.worked: Direct variation gives $V=kT$, where $k$ is constant.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: A certain amount of gas occupies $2\text{ m}^3$ when the temperature is $T=273\text{ Kelvin}$ $(=0^\circ\text{C})$. What volume will it occupy when the temperature is $T=298\text{ Kelvin}$ $(=25^\circ\text{C})$? Give your answer correct to the nearest $\text{cm}^3$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: When the gas is kept at a constant temperature, the pressure $P$ varies inversely with the volume.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Write down an equation relating $P$ and $V$.

answer.worked: Inverse variation gives $P=\frac{k}{V}$, where $k$ is constant.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: A certain amount of gas is at twice atmospheric pressure when it occupies $11.2\text{ L}$. What is the pressure when the volume is $30\text{ L}$? Express your answer as a multiple of the atmospheric pressure correct to two decimal places.

answer.worked:
Measure pressure as a multiple of atmospheric pressure and volume in litres.
$$\begin{align*}2&=\frac{k}{11.2}\\k&=22.4\\P&=\frac{22.4}{30}\\P&\approx0.75\end{align*}$$
The pressure is $0.75$ times atmospheric pressure.
